headers.//: Firebase Hosting defaults every file to max-age=3600, so for an hour after each deploy a returning visitor kept running the previous JS and CSS. The ?v= stamp in the HTML was meant to prevent that, but it is one frozen constant that never changed, and the modules import each other by bare path ('./theme.js') with no stamp at all — so a changed module kept its old URL and was served from cache. That is why newly added buttons appeared but did nothing. These files carry ETags, so no-cache costs a cheap 304 revalidation and can never serve stale code.
Content that does not change behaviour can still be cached hard.

Baseline hardening headers, applied to every response. No Content-Security-Policy here: the site loads the Firebase SDK from gstatic, talks to several *.googleapis.com/*.google-analytics.com endpoints, and embeds a Google Maps iframe on the contact page, so a CSP would need every one of those origins enumerated and verified live before it could ship without breaking sign-in or the map — worth doing, but as its own change, tested against the deployed site rather than guessed here.
